School Busing Didnt Work. And to Say So Isnt Racist.

People forget that the school busing policy worked both ways. The idea was that if you could improve poor black kid grades by busing them to rich suburban schools, you could improve inner city schools by busing in rich suburban white kids. When I was a little kid in the early 1990s, my parents found out I would be subject to the school busing policy when I went from elementary school to middle school. Every morning, I would have to take a one hour bus ride to an inner city school in the ghetto.

I never actually attended that inner city middle school because it looked so bad that my parents ended up moving to a different state altogether. So much for that societal experiment.

Very interesting article. It is important to note that policy makers sometimes make the wrong decisions in trying to solve problems.

At the end of the day it boils down to money. If we were to allow for minority students to take the bus at a later time to compensate for after school activities it would force more kids to interact, but at the same time some kids would suffer from not getting home on time.

Pretty cool to think about. If you want to read more on social psychology I recommend you read a book called "nudge".

I think they should have moved school bus times to compensate for afterschool activities. This way students would have time to interact with one another or do homework while others can participate in after school activities. Just something to consider.

Surprise Saturday discussion!

  1. Is there anything (a genre, a style, etc.) that is more better suited towards anime?
  2. Is there anything (a genre, a style, etc.) that is more better suited towards live action?
  3. Is there any live action media (TV shows, movies, that kind of thing) that you think would be better suited as an anime?

edit: Clarified question
[Discussion] Anime and Live Action - What is best suited for one or the other? What live actions would be better as anime?

1. I think Slice of Life is better animated. Also, anything that is too long to fit in a movie, and/or would require a LOT of CGI for live action. With animated stuff, since you're starting from scratch you're more free with the surroundings, and TV Shows don't have the highest CGI budgets. For example, Shinsekai Yori. Its setting is completely unique, and would require very expensive sets. The monster rats and many creatures would need to be pure CGI, and CGI would have to be used for a lot of effects, especially near the end. To solve the budget issue a movie would be practically required. However, it's ~9 hours (22 minutes not counting the ED with 25 episodes), and no-one would be willing to make a 3 or 4 part movie for a single book.
  2. Horror. With two exception (Shinsekai Yori and a certain show airing this season) I've never been scared from an anime. Although games are the real medium for horror. Also comedy, although that's more of a language issue than medium issue.
  3. I think Harry Potter might be better as an anime. As long as it doesn't have those stupid flying Death Eaters. I can't think of anything else that would be better as an anime, although there are a lot that if done well, wouldn't be worse than the live action versions.

1 and 2. For most subject matter it doesn't really matter what medium it's created in. The exception being some things (pretty much anything from battle shounen) in anime may look silly in live action. So I guess anime lends itself to making chuuni stuff look less dumb? That doesn't really limit live action though. Just the approach needs to change. A live action SAO for example would be so cringe that Kirito would need to be reworked. Long black, over designed coats look dumb. Brushing off everything looks dumb. It would be possible though.

\3. I can't really think of any because I (embarrassingly) haven't watched enough live action stuff recently. I suppose quite a bit of action movies would look cooler though.
